habitat: Usually singly in broad-leaved and riverine woodland. Largely terrestrial unless singing.
summary: A fairly common resident. A bold face pattern, with white eyebrows bordered by black lines, a white throat and a black malar streak. The breast, flanks and rump are a dull creamy orange. The immature is more mottled. The song is a loud series of repeated phrases, and it imitates other birds. The Kemp name Bearded Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: White eyebrows bordered by black lines, and a black malar streak.

underparts.pattern: Breast and flanks a dull creamy orange, the colour extending to the rump.

viewNotes.note: White eyebrows bordered by black, a white throat and a black malar streak.

calls.description: A loud series of pleasant phrases repeated three or four times, some rising in volume, and it imitates other birds. The grade A song is from Kruger near Skukuza. The filename is XC1142770-20260510_KNP_AKaramitsos_XA60_A025C036_260510PH_SLE_800HP_-3dB_Bearded-Scrub-Robin.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Creamy orange is not a colour name, so no breast or rump colour is stored. The grade A song is from Kruger. The Kemp name Bearded Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
